2.hypothesis: Lowering the fare from HK$410 to HK$380 will increase regular ticket count enough to raise total base revenue above HK$10,050, with no offsetting loss from cancellations.
2.reason: At the observed HK$410 fare, total base revenue was HK$10,050 with 24 tickets sold (18 regular, 6 background) and 5 cancellations. The panel shows strong willingness to pay at HK$410 (13 buyers, many citing budget headroom), and two declines were route/date mismatches rather than price blockers. A modest cut to HK$380 tests whether slightly lower price converts additional regular buyers without cannibalizing the existing regular base, since the discount is small relative to observed budgets.

3.hypothesis: Raising the fare from HK$410 to HK$430 will keep tickets sold near 24 and cancellations near 5, yielding total base revenue above HK$10,050.
3.reason: At HK$410 total base revenue was HK$10,050 (18 regular + 6 background tickets, 5 cancellations); cutting to HK$380 reduced revenue to HK$9,660 with identical ticket counts (24 sold, 5 cancelled), so the lower fare only cannibalized margin without adding buyers. Panel feedback shows buyers citing ample budget headroom and route/date fit rather than price as the binding constraint, and the two declines were itinerary mismatches that price cannot fix. This suggests demand is relatively inelastic in this range, so a modest increase above the observed HK$410 tests whether the same buyer count can be captured at a higher fare to lift total base revenue.
